claims.text: A controlled secondary thermal-aging treatment can induce nanoscale coherent precipitates in an equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
Secondary thermal aging can induce compositional fluctuations within the FeCoNi-based fcc matrix.
Coherent ordered precipitates can coexist with an fcc matrix in a high-entropy alloy.
Dispersed nanoscale precipitates act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Pinning caused by the precipitates hinders domain-wall motion during magnetic reversal.
Hindering domain-wall motion increases the alloy's coercivity.
The proposed starting FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy has an fcc structure.
The proposed starting alloy is almost equiatomic and has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
A homogeneous microstructure in the starting FeCoNi-based alloy results in soft ferromagnetism with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt high-entropy alloys exhibit high saturation magnetization and low coercive fields.
The low coercivity of FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt is caused by their homogeneous microstructures.
Thermal-aged samples containing coherent nanoscale precipitates will have greater coercivity than homogeneous FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt baselines.
The coercivity increase can be achieved while largely retaining high saturation magnetization.
The intervention is effective only when temperature, time, and cooling rate produce nanoscale coherent precipitates without coarse phase separation or loss of the overall fcc structure.
The magnitude of the coercivity enhancement depends on the aging-treatment parameters.
